title: Given a Scenario, Troubleshoot Common Mobile OS and Application Issues

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Mobile troubleshooting follows the same core rule as desktop troubleshooting: identify exactly what is failing before trying to fix everything.
bullets: Application launch, crashes, updates, and installation
sections.callout: App → performance → OS → power → connectivity → display.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a phone or tablet misbehaves, first determine whether the failure belongs to an application, the operating system, device performance, battery or power, connectivity, or display behavior.

sections.title: Application Fails to Launch
paragraphs: An application that fails to launch never starts successfully. Possible causes include corrupted files, insufficient storage, compatibility problems, missing permissions, a pending update, or OS incompatibility.
bullets: Check available storage and required permissions
Clear application cache or data where appropriate
sections.callout: The app never gets started → launch failure.

sections.title: Application Fails to Close or Crashes
paragraphs: An application may freeze, stop responding, close unexpectedly, or crash repeatedly after it has launched.
bullets: Clear cache or application data where appropriate
Reinstall when other targeted steps fail
sections.callout: Never opens → launch failure; opens and then fails → crash.

sections.title: Application Fails to Update
paragraphs: An existing application may fail to move to a newer version because of unavailable networking, insufficient storage, an account or store problem, an unsupported OS, corrupt application data, or a service outage.
sections.callout: The app already exists, but its new version will not install.

sections.title: Application Fails to Install
paragraphs: A new application may fail to install because the OS or device is unsupported, storage is insufficient, a device restriction or security policy blocks it, its source is untrusted, or the application-store account has a problem.
sections.callout: New app cannot be added → installation failure; existing app cannot be upgraded → update failure.

sections.title: Slow to Respond
paragraphs: A mobile device or application can remain functional but respond slowly because of low storage, excessive background applications, thermal throttling, aging hardware, malware, OS problems, or resource-intensive software.
bullets: Check battery condition and device temperature
sections.callout: It works, but sluggishly → performance issue.

sections.title: OS Fails to Update
paragraphs: A mobile operating-system update can fail because of insufficient storage, a poor network connection, low battery, unsupported hardware, corrupt update data, or management restrictions.
sections.callout: The whole mobile platform will not patch → OS update failure; one app will not patch → application update failure.

sections.title: Battery Life Issues
paragraphs: Unexpectedly short battery life means identifying what is consuming power.
sections.callout: Check per-app battery usage, screen settings, radios, synchronization, and battery health.

sections.title: Random Reboots
paragraphs: A device that restarts unexpectedly may have a failing battery, OS instability, overheating, a faulty application, a hardware problem, or a failed update.
sections.callout: The mobile device cannot stay running → random reboot symptom.

sections.title: Connectivity Issues
paragraphs: Objective 3.2 specifically separates three mobile connectivity types. Match the clue to the radio or proximity technology before changing settings.

table.caption: Mobile connectivity recognition
rows: Wireless network, SSID, access point, or WLAN

sections.title: Bluetooth Issues
paragraphs: Common Bluetooth problems include pairing failure, a device that is not discoverable, excessive distance, a disabled radio, a stale pairing, interference, or low battery.
bullets: Remove a bad pairing and pair again
sections.callout: Bluetooth → pairing, discoverability, range, and enabled state.

sections.title: Wi-Fi Issues
paragraphs: Common Wi-Fi problems include a disabled radio, the wrong network, an incorrect password, weak signal, a captive portal, router trouble, airplane mode, or an IP and DHCP problem.

sections.title: Near-Field Communication (NFC) Issues
paragraphs: NFC requires extremely short range. Failure may result from NFC being disabled, incorrect device positioning, unsupported hardware, case interference, or an incompatible application.
sections.callout: Tap-to-pay or proximity feature fails → verify NFC is enabled and position the device correctly.

sections.title: Screen Does Not Autorotate
paragraphs: Autorotation uses orientation sensors to rotate the display. If the screen works but remains in one orientation, check rotation lock, application rotation support, the sensor, and the operating system.
sections.callout: Turn the device and the screen should follow; check autorotate or rotation lock first.

table.caption: Classify the symptom before choosing an action
rows: Does it fail to launch, crash, install, or update?
Is the device or application slow? Is storage low?
Does the platform update fail or behave unstably?
Is battery life poor or does the device reboot?
Is the clue Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or NFC?
Does the screen fail to autorotate?

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: App never opens → application launch failure
App closes or freezes after opening → application crash
Existing app will not get a new version → application update failure
New app will not install → application installation failure
Mobile platform will not patch → OS update failure
Device drains quickly → battery life issue
Peripheral will not pair → Bluetooth issue
Cannot join a WLAN → Wi-Fi issue
Display will not change orientation → autorotation issue

sections.title: Objective 3.2 Exam Trap
bullets: An app that never opens has a launch failure; one that opens and then stops has crashed.
An application update affects one existing app; an OS update affects the whole mobile platform.
Installation adds a new app; an update replaces an existing version.
Bluetooth clues involve pairing and peripheral range; NFC clues involve tapping and very close proximity.
SSID, Wi-Fi password, access point, and WLAN clues point to Wi-Fi.
If the display works but will not change orientation, check autorotation or rotation lock before assuming screen hardware failure.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Opens and then dies → app crash
Existing app will not patch → app update failure
New app will not load → app installation failure
Platform will not patch → OS update failure
Drains too quickly → battery life issue
Will not change portrait and landscape orientation → autorotation
sections.callout: App → performance → OS → power → connectivity → display.
